title: He was in the room, and His testimony is enough
subtitle: Ash-Shahid: the Witness, present to every event and the final word on what is true
intro: Ash-Shahid (الشَّهِيدُ) means the Witness: the One who is present to everything that happens, from whom nothing is ever absent, and whose testimony about what really happened is perfect and final. It means you never need another witness to be believed, and no truth is lost because no one else was there.

root.sense: Shuhud is presence: to be there and see it with your own eyes. Shahadah is testimony: to declare what you saw. The root joins being present and bearing witness. Ash-Shahid is never absent from anything, and what He testifies is the truth itself.

row.title: No one saw, so no one will know
sub: it is my word against theirs

knowing: Ash-Shahid is present to all things. Scholars explain that Al-Alim is His knowledge of everything, and when that knowledge is joined to the outward, visible events of the world, He is called Ash-Shahid. {idea}Nothing is ever absent from Him, and nothing happens out of His sight.{/idea} Every conversation, every agreement, every quiet injustice and every quiet kindness takes place in His presence.

Three names meet here. Al-Basir is His sight. Ar-Raqib is His watch over you, guarding and keeping account. Ash-Shahid is His presence and testimony: He is the witness who will declare what truly happened. Human witnesses forget, take sides or only see part of the event. His witness is complete and fair.

He is also the Witness to the truth itself. Allah bears witness that the message is from Him (4:166), and He asks: is it not enough that your Lord is Witness over all things (41:53)? {idea}His own testimony is the strongest proof there is.{/idea}
seeing: When Musa agreed to work for the old man of Madyan in return for marriage, he closed the deal with the words: Allah is witness over what we say (28:28). Yaqub did the same when his sons gave him their promise (12:66). Believers have always placed their agreements before the One who is present to every word.

Isa will say on the Last Day that he was a witness over his people only while he was with them, but Allah is Witness over all things (5:117). And on that Day Allah will tell people what they did. He kept count of it while they forgot it, and He is Witness over all things (58:6).

In the story of the believers burned in a ditch, the oppressors sat watching and enjoying it. Surah al-Buruj ends that scene by reminding us that Allah, to whom belongs the heavens and the earth, is Witness over all things (85:9). The crime had an audience of tyrants, but it also had a Witness they could not escape.
trusting: Some of the hardest pain comes from wrongs that no one else saw: abuse behind closed doors, a lie told about you, a promise broken in private. {reward}Ash-Shahid was there.{/reward} You do not need to collect evidence to be believed by Him, and the truth of what happened is preserved with Him exactly.

This name also brings peace when you are misunderstood. You can stop exhausting yourself trying to prove your innocence to everyone. Do what is right, say what is true, and let Allah be enough as Witness (4:79).

And it guards you. {trap}Treating private promises and quiet dealings as if they do not count{/trap} is how trust breaks down. When you know He was present at every agreement, you keep your word even when no court could hold you to it.
loving: We feel close to those who were there for us, who were present on the worst night and the best day. Ash-Shahid has been present at every moment of your life. {idea}You have never been through anything alone.{/idea}
It is a comfort to love the One whose testimony about you is fair: He saw your weakness, but He also saw every effort no one else noticed.
now: You come out of a meeting where a colleague took credit for your work and quietly blamed you for their mistake. No one else knows what really happened. {idea}Ash-Shahid was in that room, and He saw every detail.{/idea} Say what is true calmly, then let it rest with the Witness who misses nothing.
old: If there is no proof, the truth about what happened will never come out.
new: Ash-Shahid was present for all of it, and His witness is enough for me.
try: Keep one promise today exactly as you said it, especially one no one else would ever check.

dua.text: Ya Shahid, You were present when I was wronged and when I did wrong. Be my Witness for every truth I spoke, and forgive what You saw of my failings.
dua.note: Call on Him by this name when making agreements or when no one else saw what happened; Musa sealed his agreement with Allah is witness over what we say (28:28).

pairs.why: Ar-Raqib watches over every moment; Ash-Shahid is present to it and testifies to its truth (5:117).
Ash-Shahid bears witness and Al-Haqq is the Truth; His testimony is truth itself, so nothing false survives before Him.
Al-Muhsi counts every deed and Ash-Shahid was present to each one; nothing is forgotten and nothing is misremembered (58:6).

faq.a: Ash-Shahid means the Witness. Allah is present to everything that happens, nothing is ever absent from Him, and His testimony about what truly happened is complete and final. He is also the Witness to the truth of His message.

faq.q: Is Ash-Shahid the same as shaheed, a martyr?
faq.a: They share the same root, which means presence and witnessing, but they are different. Ash-Shahid as a name of Allah means the One who witnesses all things. A martyr is called shaheed for other reasons explained by scholars, such as being witnessed by the angels or bearing witness to the truth with his life.

faq.q: What is the difference between Ash-Shahid and Al-Basir?
faq.a: Al-Basir is His perfect sight: nothing escapes it. Ash-Shahid adds presence and testimony: He is present at every event and will bear true witness to it on the Day of Judgement. Both are real attributes affirmed as befits His majesty.
